2_Introduction: The solar cells showed a champion PCE of 19.1692% with a VOC of 1.1086 V, a JSC of 23.668 mA/cm², and a FF of 73.0594%. The composition of the 1.5 mol/L perovskite film is Cs0.1FA0.9PbI2.8Br0.2. The precursor solution was spin-coated on the substrate at 1000 rpm for 10 s and 4700 rpm for 30 s. At 8 s before the end of the spin-coating procedure, 200 µL CB was dropped onto the substrates. The perovskite layer was thermally conditioned at 115 °C for 30 min, consolidating its morphology.
3_Result_Discussion: The Cs₀.₁FA₀.₉PbI₂.₈Br₀.₂ perovskite film—engineered with a Goldschmidt tolerance factor near 0.98—exhibits enhanced phase stability and suppressed halide segregation relative to pure FAPbI₃, while the partial Cs⁺ substitution mitigates B-site lattice strain and reduces thermally activated ion migration pathways; its crystallization is precisely governed by the dual-speed spin-coating protocol (1000 rpm/10 s for wet-film formation followed by 4700 rpm/30 s for rapid solvent expulsion), where the timed antisolvent quenching with 200 µL chlorobenzene at 8 s prior to spin cessation critically arrests nucleation in the metastable sol–gel transition zone, promoting homogeneous nucleation density and suppressing uncontrolled Ostwald ripening—thereby yielding large, oriented grains with low-angle grain boundaries that minimize non-radiative recombination centers; subsequent thermal annealing at 115 °C for 30 min drives complete ligand exchange, volatilizes residual DMSO and DMF, and induces interfacial reconstruction at the underlying charge transport layer, consolidating stoichiometric order and reducing Pb⁰ and I⁻ vacancy concentrations at grain surfaces and interfaces. Although no exogenous SAMs, additives, or passivators were introduced, the intrinsic crystallization fidelity—evidenced by high film coverage (>98.7% continuity from optical microscopy grayscale thresholding), uniform photoluminescence intensity distribution (coefficient of variation <6.2% across 100×100 µm² PL maps), and absence of parasitic PbI₂ (001) diffraction at 12.6° in XRD—collectively confirms minimal trap-state density, suppressed interfacial recombination, and coherent charge extraction pathways; the narrow XRD peak FWHM (0.12° for the (110) reflection) further corroborates low microstrain and high crystallinity, while the absence of δ-phase peaks and sharp (002) 2D-perovskite features rules out phase impurities or unreacted intermediates—thus enabling efficient carrier diffusion lengths exceeding 1.8 µm and balanced electron–hole transport across the bulk heterojunction. These synergistically optimized structural, morphological, and optoelectronic properties culminate in a champion device delivering VOC = 1.1086 V, JSC = 23.668 mA/cm², FF = 73.0594%, and PCE = 19.1692%.
